[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u2709\ufe0fCommunications Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The communications module contains features related to personal interactions within (and without) the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcddLetters", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3Bta1pYT8D", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Letters received by the church from church people or missionaries can be added to the relevant person or missionary for archival or reference purposes.

When adding a letter to a person or missionary, note the following:
- Check the 'Is Private' checkbox if the letter is not to be displayed publicly.
    - Missionary letters will be displayed on the public 'missions' website page unless this checkbox is checked!
- If the letter should be shared with the church, check the 'Share with Church?' checkbox
    - Once the letter is shared, the 'Shared Date' field should be updated
    - The Letters To Be Shared With Church report will show all letters that should be, and have not yet been shared with the church.

Example Workflow:
1. Missionary Mike sends a prayer letter that he would like read to the church.
2. The Church Secretary receives the letter, navigates to `Missions > Missionaries > Missionary Mike > Letters to the Church` and adds the letter to the Missionary Mike document making note that the letter should be read to the church.
3. Before the next church service, the Pastor runs the `Missions > Missionary Letters` report and filters by 'Share w/ Church` to see which letters need to be read.
4. The letters are added to the `Event Schedule` for the next `Function` (Service).
5. Missionary Mike's `Missionary` document can be updated with a date to show that the letter was read to the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulHeading01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcf0Bulletins", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulIntro0001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Bulletin is the printed handout for one function: a Letter sheet printed on both sides and folded in half. The front cover carries the church name, the function name, the date, a cover image, and a verse of the week. The inside and back hold whichever sections you switch on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulCreate001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To create a bulletin, open the function and choose 'Create -> Bulletin', or add a Bulletin and pick the function. The new bulletin starts with:
- The sections switched on in Bulletin Settings. Switch any of them off for this bulletin only; a section with nothing to print is left out automatically.
- The Missionary of the Week, picked in turn (week by week, in title order) from the missionaries whose Status is not Inactive and whose support has not ended. Change it for this bulletin if you like. Missionaries marked as sensitive are never picked, and are refused, unless 'Include Sensitive Missionaries' is on in Bulletin Settings.
- Every open prayer request that is not private. Remove the rows you do not want printed; private requests cannot be added.
- Attach a cover image, type a verse of the week, such as John 3:16, and write the welcome message and announcements.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulChurchSect1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More than one church. Add a row under Sections Per Church in Bulletin Settings to give a church its own bulletin. A row replaces the whole set for that church rather than changing one part of it, so tick every section you want in it; a new row starts with the same options as the settings above. The Church Roles list is shared: it says which job titles the leadership section prints, such as Pastor or Elder. Who appears under them is always that church's own people, so each congregation's bulletin names its own pastor.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulSections1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What the automatic sections print:
- Order of Worship: the function's schedule, with times and the titles of linked songs, sermons and other items.
- Church Leadership: the church roles chosen in Bulletin Settings, with the people who hold those positions on the function date.
- Upcoming: functions in the days after the function date (how many days is set in Bulletin Settings).
- Ministries: active ministries and their mission statements.
- Birthdays and Anniversaries: from the function date for the number of days set in Bulletin Settings, for active members or everyone. Names and days only; no ages or years. People with 'Hide from Directory and Bulletin' ticked on their Person record are left out, and so is a couple's anniversary when either of them is. People who have a 'Death' life event are left out too, and so is a couple's anniversary when either spouse has died.
- Church Verse: the verse set on the Church record, printed at the foot of the back cover. Like the verse of the week, it prints with its words in the church's Default Bible Translation once that translation has its text, and as the reference alone until then.
- Church Image: the image (such as a logo) set on the Church record, printed above the church name on the front cover.
- Contact Information: the church address, phone, email and website from the Church record. A branch that leaves its website blank prints its parent church's website. A blank phone or email falls back to Contact Us Settings.
- Sermon Handout Insert: when a sermon on the schedule has a Sermon Handout, a third sheet prints it twice, to cut into two half-page inserts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulPrint0001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Printing: click 'Print Bulletin' and download the PDF. Print it double-sided on Letter paper, flipped on the short edge, and fold it in half. Each panel has fixed space, so shorten a section or switch one off if text is cut off. For the handout sheet, print half as many copies and cut them down the dashed line.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulOnline001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Share a bulletin online. Tick Show in Portal on a bulletin to share it with your members. Members who log in see it on the Bulletins page. They can read it in the browser or download the PDF. A member sees only the bulletins of their own church. Visitors who are not logged in go to the login page first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bulAnnounce1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Public announcements. To show the announcements to everyone, tick Show in Portal and Show Announcements on the Website. The public Announcements page shows the announcements of the five newest bulletins that have both boxes ticked. It shows nothing else from the bulletin: no welcome, no prayer requests, no birthdays and no order of worship. An image that you add to shared announcements is public. If the announcements hold an image that you added before you ticked the box, remove it and add it again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "X5XpRUgRXI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udda5\ufe0fPresentations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Nvk4J2JbSr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Presentations are the slides of a Sermon, shown at a church event. Click 'Present' on a sermon to show its slides full screen in the browser. To present songs, or for more advanced use-cases, we recommend FreeShow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MtTk2oxuSy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a sermon, note the following:
- Add as many slides as needed containing the content you would like to display.
- You may want to add the sermon as an item in a church event's schedule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "present_public_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Presentations on the public website. A visitor who is not signed in sees only Scripture slides, published Beliefs, and published Missionaries that are not marked Sensitive. A Belief or Missionary slide shows only the fields that the Beliefs and Missions pages show. Every other slide, such as a Song or a Person, shows \"This slide is not public\". A signed-in user sees the whole slide when they can open its record, with only the fields they can read. Otherwise they see what a visitor sees.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailHead", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u2709\ufe0fChurch Emails", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailIntro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Church Email sends one message to many people at once, by email or by text message. Each person gets their own copy, so no one sees the other addresses or numbers. Only a Church Manager can send one. Other staff can read the ones that were sent.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailSend", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To send one:
1. Add a Church Email. You can also open a Group and click 'Actions -> Send Church Email', or tick people in the Person list and click 'Actions -> New Church Email'.
2. In 'Send As', choose Email or Text Message.
3. In 'Send To', choose who gets it:
    - Active People: everyone whose Status is Active, whatever their Membership.
    - Active Members: only the people whose Membership is Member and whose Status is Active.
    - Group: the members of one Group, whatever their Status.
    - Smart List: the people on a saved list of people or a saved Attendance Count. Churchit reads the list when it sends the message.
    - Chosen People: only the people you put in 'People'.
    Check 'Include Their Households' to also send the message to the people in the Family of each person above. In 'Household Members', choose Everyone, Adults, or Adults and Other Adults. Churchit adds only living people of the message's church, and each person gets one copy. Each added person must also allow the purpose.
4. In 'Purpose', choose what the message is about, for example Church News or Pastoral Care. Only people who allow that purpose get it.
5. For an email, write the Subject and the Message. To start from an Email Template, pick it in 'Template'. This fills in the Subject and the Message, and you can change them after. To send files with an email, save it and attach them in the sidebar. For a text message, write the 'Text'. Up to 160 characters is one text.
6. Click 'Preview' to see the message as one person gets it.
7. Click 'Send Test Email' or 'Send Test Text' to get a copy yourself.
8. Click 'Send'. Churchit tells you how many people it goes to and asks you to confirm.
To send it later, set 'Send At' before you click Send. It is sent within a few minutes of that time. Until then, 'Unschedule' turns it back into a draft.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailPlace", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A placeholder puts each person's own name into the message. Write it in double braces, for example \"Dear {{ first_name }},\". You can use these placeholders: {{ first_name }}, {{ last_name }}, {{ display_name }} and {{ full_name }}. Email Templates write the same names as {{ doc.first_name }}, and that works too. You can use placeholders in the Subject, the Message and the Text. Churchit does not save a message that uses any other placeholder, and it tells you which ones you can use.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailPreview", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "'Preview' shows the message for the first person it goes to: their address or number, the subject, and the message with the placeholders filled in. To see it for someone else, pick them in 'Person'. The preview also shows how many people get the message, and for a text, how many characters it has.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailWho", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who gets it is worked out when it is sent, so people who joined or left since you wrote it are counted correctly. Churchit leaves out people who have a 'Death' life event and people who do not allow the Purpose. It also leaves out people with no email address, an email address marked Email Bounced, or an email address that unsubscribed. A household that shares one email address or phone number gets one copy. After it is sent, 'Sent To' shows how many people it went to, and the Church Email can no longer be changed. If sending stops, the Church Email goes back to Draft and a comment on it says why. If sending takes longer than the time allowed, the Church Email stays Sending and continues by itself about 15 minutes later. When you send it again, only the people who did not get it yet get it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailCopies", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each copy shows on the timeline of the person's Person form, with the subject and message as they got them. The Church Email lists the copies it sent in its own timeline.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailText", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A text message goes to each person's primary phone number. It goes only to people who said yes to texts. Nothing can be sent as a text until the SMS Settings are set up. To send texts, a user must be a System Manager or have a role in the Allowed Roles of the SMS Settings.
Churchit checks each text after it sends it. If your text provider (for example, Twilio) refuses a text, or the text is not in the SMS Log, Churchit marks that copy Error on the timeline of the person and of the message. A copy that left is marked Sent. Sent To counts only the texts that left. Churchit does not send a refused text again, also when you send the message again. To find the reason, look at the log of your text provider. Correct the number on the Person, then send a new message to that person. If the provider refuses every text, for example because of a wrong password, sending stops and the message becomes a draft again. When you send it again, only the people who did not get it receive it. A provider can accept a text and block it later, for example when a carrier filters it. Churchit cannot see this, so look for these texts in the log of your provider.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chEmailUnsub", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every email has an 'Unsubscribe' link at the bottom. For Church News, a person who clicks it gets no more Church Emails from your church. For another purpose, the person stops getting emails for that purpose only. Members can also change their choices on the Communication Preferences page in the portal. When someone without a portal login asks to get Church Emails again, open their Person and click 'Resubscribe to Church Emails'. Nothing can be sent by email until an outgoing Email Account is set up. With multi-church on, a Church Email goes only to the people of its own church. Only that church's groups, smart lists and people can be picked.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bounceHead", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Bounced Emails", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bounceBody", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When an email cannot reach an address, the mail server sends a report back to the church. This report is a bounce. Churchit reads bounces only when the church's email account receives mail. Open the Email Account that sends the church's email and tick Enable Incoming. The bounce goes back to the account that sent the email, so this account must send and receive. Churchit reads the bounces that Gmail, Microsoft 365 and Postfix mail servers send. It can miss a bounce from a different mail server.
When a bounce says that delivery failed, Churchit ticks Email Bounced on that address on every record that has it, such as a Person or a Family. Churchit does this only for an address that the church sent an email to in the last 7 days, because anyone can send an email that looks like a bounce. A bounce that says a rule blocked the email (a code that starts with 5.7) or that the mailbox is full (5.2.2) changes nothing. Church Emails do not send to that address. For a bounce from Gmail or Microsoft 365, the delivery status of the sent email also changes to Bounced. A bounce that says only that delivery is late changes nothing.
To find bounced addresses, open the People Data Quality report and set Problem to Email Bounced. Ask the person for a new address. When you change the address, Churchit clears Email Bounced. If you know that the address works again, untick Email Bounced on that row.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "openHead", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who opened an email", "col": 12}}, {"id": "openBody", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit can show who opened a Church Email. On the Email Account that sends the church's email, Track Email Status is ticked by default. Then each copy of an email has a small image that the reader cannot see. When the reader's mail app loads the image, the copy shows Read on the timeline of the person's Person form and on the timeline of the Church Email.
Many mail apps do not load images until the reader allows them. Then a person can read an email, and their copy does not show Read. So the number of Read copies is less than the number of people who read the email. Some mail apps, such as Apple Mail, load all images when the email arrives. Then the copy shows Read also when the person did not open it.
To stop this tracking, open the Email Account and untick Track Email Status. The emails that you send after this have no image. If you keep the tracking, tell people about it in the church's privacy notice.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "smsStopHead", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Text replies and STOP", "col": 12}}, {"id": "smsStopBody", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit sends text messages, but it does not receive the replies. Your text provider gets them. So use a text provider that handles STOP replies itself. Twilio, for example, does this by default for numbers in the US and Canada. To change the keywords and the reply, put the number in a Twilio Messaging Service, turn on Advanced Opt-Out, and send your texts with that Messaging Service. In other countries, and with other providers, read the provider's opt-out rules. When a person replies STOP, the provider blocks every later text to that number. The person replies START to get texts again.
Churchit does not know about a STOP reply, so it continues to send texts to that number. The provider refuses them, and Churchit marks each of these copies Error. When a person asks you to stop their texts, record it in Churchit: add a Communication Consent for the person with the channel SMS and the status Withdrawn. Leave Purpose blank to stop texts for all purposes. A member can also turn off the Text switches on the Communication Preferences page.
This applies to every text that Churchit sends: Church Emails sent as text messages, group messages sent as texts, Page Parents at check-in, and volunteer requests and reminders. A message that also goes by email, such as a page to the parents, then goes to the person by email. A Notification that sends a text also stops at the provider after STOP, but Churchit keeps no copy of it to mark Error. To find these texts, look in the Error Log or in the provider's log.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "consentHead", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u2705Consent", "col": 12}}, {"id": "consentWhat", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each person can say yes or no to being contacted by email, text message, push notification, phone or post. A Communication Consent records one answer: the person, the channel, a purpose (or blank for every purpose), Given or Withdrawn, when they said it and how. You cannot change a consent after you save it. If someone changes their mind, click Record a Change of Mind and save the new answer. The newest answer is the one that counts. A yes for every purpose does not undo a no for one purpose. To start that purpose again, record a yes for that purpose. When two answers have the same date and time, the one saved last counts. Recorded On cannot be in the future. A person's consents are listed on the Connections tab of their Person form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "consentPurpose", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Communication Purpose is a reason the church contacts people, such as Church News, Pastoral Care or Child Safety. A person can say yes to one purpose and no to another. A Church Email has Church News unless you choose another Purpose, and a page to parents from the Check-In Station has Child Safety, so you cannot delete these two. Reminders of a function sign-up have Event Registrations, and ministry team requests and reminders have Serving. You cannot delete these either. A person gets a ministry team text only with text consent for Serving, but the ministry team emails go to everyone asked to serve. You can add your own purposes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "consentAsk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the UK, the EU and other places, the law says people must agree before a church contacts them. In that case, tick Contact People Only With Their Consent on the Church. The church then contacts only people who said yes. When the box is not ticked, the church contacts people until they say no. The church never contacts a person who has died.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "consentRenew", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Asking people to renew their consent: A church that ticks Contact People Only With Their Consent can ask people to confirm, from time to time, that they still want its emails. Open Notifications, duplicate \"Consent Renewal\" and turn on the copy. Two years (730 days) after a person last said yes to email, the copy emails their primary email address with a Yes, keep in touch link. The person needs no login. The link records a new yes, with How set to Email Link, for each email purpose the person allows. Their choices do not change, and the next reminder comes two years after that. Each yes asks only once: if the person does nothing, Churchit does not ask again until they next change their choices. To ask after a different time, change Days After on your copy. People in a church that does not tick the box, people who said no last, and people who have died get no reminder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "consentTexts", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Texts need a yes first: A person gets text messages only after they say yes to texts. This is true also when Contact People Only With Their Consent is not ticked. A person can say yes on the Communication Preferences page, on a Connection Card, or to you. To record a yes that a person tells you, add a Communication Consent with the channel SMS. Push notifications also need a yes first, with the channel Push.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "consentUnsub", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When someone clicks Unsubscribe in a Church News email, or turns off Church News by email on the Communication Preferences page, everyone at your church who uses that email address is recorded as having said no to Church News. The link in an email with another Purpose records a no to that Purpose only. A Church Email leaves out everyone who said no to its Purpose. When you resubscribe someone from their Person form, only that person is recorded as having said yes.
Automatic emails and text messages (Notifications) leave out an address only when no person who uses it may be contacted. Staff always get the work notices meant for them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "consentPrefs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Communication Preferences: Signed-in members choose how the church may contact them on the Communication Preferences page in the portal. The page shows their primary email address and phone number, and one row for each Communication Purpose. Each row has an Email switch. It also has a Text switch when text messages are set up in SMS Settings and the member has a phone number, and a Push switch when the member allowed notifications on a device (see Notifications on Phones). A switch saves at once. It records a consent for that member only, with How set to Member Portal. If a member stopped every email to their address, the page tells them. When they turn on an email switch, emails to that address start again. A member with no email address on file sees a note that asks them to contact the church office.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "consentCards", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Connection Cards: The Stay in Touch section of the Connection Card has two boxes: Email Me Church News and Events, and Text Me Church News and Events. The text box shows after the guest types a phone number. When Churchit processes the card, each ticked box records a yes to Church News for the card's person, with How set to Web Form. A ticked box records nothing when the card has no email address or phone number for it, when the card is Spam, or when the card is linked to a person who does not already have that email address or phone number. A phone number matches when it has the same digits as one on the person. A ticked box does not replace a no that the person gave before. A paper card that you add in the desk works the same way.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pushHead", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcf1Notifications on Phones", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pushIntro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit can show notifications on a member's phone or computer, through the installed member app or the browser. The site sends them itself with Web Push, so you do not need an outside push service. No feature sends push notifications yet. When a feature sends them, only members who allowed notifications on a device and turned on Push for that purpose get one. Everyone else gets the message by email or text, where the feature sends those.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pushSetup", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Set it up: A System Manager opens Push Settings. Type the Contact Address as mailto: and the church office email, for example mailto:office@example.org, and save. Click Generate Keys once. Then tick Enabled and save. Do not remove the keys later, because each browser that allowed notifications uses them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pushMembers", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Allow notifications on a device: A member opens the Communication Preferences page and clicks Allow notifications. The browser then asks them to allow notifications. The member does this on each phone or computer. Turn off stops notifications on that device. On an iPhone or iPad, the member must first add the site to the Home Screen and open it from there. This needs iOS 16.4 or later. When a browser stops accepting notifications, Churchit forgets that browser. A member who signs in on a shared device and allows notifications takes that device over from the person before them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pushConsent", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Push needs a yes first: After a member allows notifications on a device, the Communication Preferences page shows a Push switch for each purpose. Each switch is off until the member turns it on, as for texts. Staff can also record a yes or a no on a Communication Consent with the channel Push.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chatHead", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcacStaff Chat", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chatBody", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit has no chat. For chat between staff, a System Manager can install Raven on the same site. Raven is a free Frappe app with the AGPL license. Only a person with the Raven User role can use Raven. A member who has only the Church User role does not have this role and has no desk, so they cannot use it. To send a message to the members of a group, a leader uses Message the group on the Lead a Group page in the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chatInstall", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Install Raven. On your own server, run bench get-app --branch main https://github.com/frappe/raven, then bench --site your site install-app raven. On Frappe Cloud, add Raven to the bench and install it on the site. Churchit refuses to install with an app that has a doctype with the same name as a Churchit doctype. Raven has no such doctype, so the install continues.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chatChurches", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More than one church. Raven does not follow the church rules of Churchit. Each Raven user sees the name, photo and phone number of all other Raven users on the site, and can send a direct message to each of them. Raven workspaces do not change this. A person in a Raven channel sees all of its messages, also the messages from staff of a different church. So give Raven access only to staff who may see, and be seen by, the staff of all churches. Right after you install Raven, open Raven Settings and turn off 'Automatically add system users to Raven'. If it stays on, Raven adds each desk user when their User record is saved. Then give the Raven User role, or the Raven User role profile, by hand to each person who may use Raven. To stop a person, remove the role. Make one Raven workspace for each church. Set its Type to Private and tick 'Can only join via invite?'. Then add the staff of that church to it by hand.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "chatRecords", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Private records. A Raven Document Notification copies the text of a record into a chat message. Everyone in the channel can read that message, also people who cannot open the record. Do not set a Document Notification on Person, Person Note, Care Request, Counseling Case, Prayer Request or Background Check.", "col": 12}}]
